title: Why Some People Would Rather Lose Everything Than Change? - Thursday: Maamar Yafeh Sha'ah Achas #6
blurb: The Secret of Moshiach: You Can Never Be Free Until You Let Go of Who You Think You Are Why do some people continue destroying their marriages, families, careers, and relationships through addiction, even after losing almost everything? Why can one person recognize their wounds and seek healing, while another seems completely incapable of recognizing that anything is wrong? In this extraordinary class, the Mitteler Rebbe introduces two profoundly different forms of emotional and spiritual woundedness. In the first, a person may be shattered, overwhelmed, and trapped in destructive patterns, yet a healthy core remains accessible. Indeed, the very fact that they seek help reveals an inner self that is still protesting the pain and refusing to accept the disconnection. But there exists a second, far more devastating condition: when a person becomes so identified with their survival mechanisms, cravings, and counterfeit sources of vitality that their very sense of "I" is replaced by a false identity. Their addictions are no longer merely things they do; they have become who they believe they are. Like a mother willing to endure unimaginable suffering rather than release her beloved child, this person clings desperately to what feels like their only source of life—unaware that the child they are protecting is made of wax, while their real child is waiting at home.
